papers.title: When uncertainty quantification fails: structural vulnerabilities and corrections for selective prediction under clinical class imbalance
papers.abstract: Background. Selective prediction systems improve the safety of clinical artificial intelligence by deferring ambiguous cases to human experts while automating high-confidence decisions. However, this safety mechanism relies entirely on the premise that uncertainty scores accurately reflect clinical ambiguity. In prognostic tasks characterized by severe class imbalance, where the clinical outcome of interest is a minority, this assumption breaks down. Standard uncertainty measures cease to capture clinically aligned ambiguity; instead, they become a proxy for class membership, systematically penalizing minority patients regardless of their individual predictive clarity. Results. Across 56 synthetic conditions and three neurodegenerative cohorts spanning severe class imbalance to near-balanced conditions (multiple sclerosis, Parkinson's Disease, Alzheimer's Disease), our framework consistently maintained bounded, balanced risk across trajectories. In contrast, global metrics either collapsed minority Sensitivity or protected the minority at the expense of majority patients. Applying CCR with standard entropy fails to protect the minority because it breaks within-class monotonicity when tau=0.5. Combining CCR with threshold-aware metrics restores strict monotonicity, correctly identifies ambiguous patients, and safely mitigates minority exclusion. Conclusions. Under clinical class imbalance, standard uncertainty quantification measures dataset sparsity rather than clinical ambiguity, creating a systemic illusion of safety. This bias is a correctable structural flaw. Clinical pipelines deploying selective prediction under imbalance should adopt threshold-aligned uncertainty measures and class-stratified evaluation. This reduces class-specific risk imbalance, supporting safer selective prediction under the evaluated conditions without silently excluding the most vulnerable patients.
authors: For the Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative

papers.title: Biomaterials and biofabrication in the Netherlands: state of the art in 2026
papers.abstract: Biomaterials and biofabrication are multidisciplinary and rapidly evolving fields that enable innovations that are crucial for addressing current healthcare challenges. The Netherlands has a broad, active, and collaborative research community that is developing advanced biomaterials and cutting.edge biofabrication methods, with applications in tissue engineering, regenerative medicine, in vitro disease modeling, and biomedical devices. Dutch researchers have pioneered advanced biofabrication, supramolecular and inorganic chemistry for creating biomaterials, organoids and organ-on-chip in vitro platforms, and regenerative medicine. This paper presents recent work on biomaterials and biofabrication and their applications from 11 prominent research institutions across the Netherlands, and it describes joint initiatives that target broader goals within the field. Contributors from each institution provide insights into recent progress, key scientific contributions, and forward-looking perspectives. By presenting the state-of-the-art research landscape, this article serves as a reference for scientists actively engaged in or planning to initiate biofabrication or biomaterials-related research, offering guidance on technology selection, experimental design, academic collaboration, and translational development.

papers.title: Penguatan Literasi Membaca Siswa SD melalui Pembelajaran Kreatif Berbasis Cerita Lokal Bernilai Keagamaan di Desa Muktiwari, Cibitung, Bekasi
papers.abstract: Reading literacy remains a major challenge in improving the quality of primary education in Indonesia, particularly in rural areas, including Muktiwari Village, Bekasi Regency. Although the village has a Multicultural Village Library and the “Ayo Gemar Membaca” (Let’s Love Reading) program, their use has not been optimal because literacy instruction remains conventional, reading materials based on local wisdom are limited, and religious values have not been systematically integrated into literacy activities. This community service program aimed to strengthen elementary students’ reading literacy through creative multimedia-based learning using local stories with religious values. The program was conducted in May–June 2026 and involved 66 fifth-grade students in Muktiwari Village. It comprised socialization and needs assessment, program preparation, learning implementation, mentoring and evaluation, and sustainability planning. The learning activities included reading motivation, an artificial intelligence (AI)-based animated film entitled Nawawi Sang Penebar Kebaikan, an interactive Stop and Thinking role play, and a literacy treasure hunt. Evaluation was conducted through observation, interviews, and analysis of Group Worksheets (LKK). Most students responded positively, understood the story and its religious values, and all groups completed the worksheets correctly. These results indicate that integrating AI-based multimedia, local stories, active learning, and religious values creates a more engaging, contextual, and meaningful literacy experience. The program also produced modules, learning media, and literacy tools recommended for integration into the School Literacy Movement (GLS) and the “Ayo Gemar Membaca” program to ensure sustainability.

papers.title: Enhancing diagnostic ability in oral mucosal lesions using a flipped classroom and audience response system
papers.abstract: Objective To evaluate whether a flipped classroom–based online course supported by active learning tools improves diagnostic performance and self-confidence for diagnosing oral lesions among undergraduate dental students. Methods A 14-week online course on oral mucosal lesion diagnosis was conducted between August and December 2021 with 27 undergraduate dental students. The course adopted a flipped classroom model, combining asynchronous learning with weekly 90-minute synchronous sessions focused on clinical case discussions. An audience response system was used to promote active participation. The syllabus covered common oral mucosal lesions, including ulcers, nodules, erosions, and plaques. Educational effectiveness was assessed using a pre- and posttest design based on a 30-item image-based quiz that required classification of lesions as benign, potentially malignant, or malignant. Participants’ self-confidence was assessed using a two-item Likert-scale instrument adapted from previous studies that measured confidence in diagnosing oral lesions. Moreover, students’ perceptions of the teaching strategy were evaluated through a post-course questionnaire. Results A significant improvement in diagnostic performance was observed after course completion ( p < 0.01, Wilcoxon test), with a mean increase of 25.1% in correct answers. Self-confidence increased significantly, with the proportion of participants reporting being very confident rising from 11.1% ( n = 3) to 70.4% ( n = 19) ( p < 0.05). Students reported high acceptance of the instructional approach: 96.3% found the audience response system enjoyable and conducive to active engagement, and 100.0% indicated that it enhanced understanding of the content. Conclusion An online flipped classroom approach combined with active learning tools effectively improved diagnostic accuracy and engagement in oral mucosal lesion education. Clinical relevance Strengthening undergraduate training in oral mucosal lesion diagnosis may enhance dentists’ ability and self-confidence to recognize clinically relevant conditions, supporting earlier referral and improved patient care.

papers.title: A parameterized data-driven neural network with physics-based regularization for thermal field prediction in metal additive manufacturing
papers.abstract: Laser Powder Bed Fusion (L-PBF) is a metal additive manufacturing process characterized by highly transient and localized thermal behavior that strongly influences melt pool evolution and the resulting material properties. Accurate prediction of the spatiotemporal temperature field is therefore essential for process optimization, but conventional numerical simulations remain computationally expensive for large parametric studies. In this work, a parameterized data-driven neural network with physics-based regularization is developed for predicting transient thermal fields in SS316L across varying laser power and scan speed conditions. The framework incorporates process parameters directly into the input space together with spatiotemporal coordinates, enabling continuous thermal prediction within the bounded process domain. High-fidelity finite element method (FEM) thermal simulations provide the primary supervision, while the transient heat conduction equation is incorporated as a physics-based regular- ization term during training. The proposed framework achieves an RMSE of 9.01 K while accurately predicting thermal fields and melt pool geometry.

papers.title: Inverse Design of Polyarylate Nanofiber‐Enabled Basalt Scale Nanocomposite Insulating Paper for High Dielectric Reliability via Finite Element‐Guided Machine Learning
papers.abstract: The dielectric reliability of polymer‐based insulating paper critically depends on whether its structure–property relationships can be predicted and programmatically tuned. However, most dielectric papers are still developed through empirical trial‐and‐error, which limits precise design and efficient optimization toward target performance metrics. Here we establish a digitally enabled inverse design framework that integrates finite element analysis (FEA) with machine learning (ML) to enable the predictable fabrication of high‐performance γ‐BS/PAR nanofiber composite insulating paper (γ‐BS: silane‐modified basalt scales; PAR: polyarylate nanofibers). A physics‐based structure–property dataset was generated via microstructure‐resolved FEA and used to train an ML surrogate that not only predicts breakdown strength but also inversely recommends process/structure parameters within a feasible processing window. Guided by the model, the optimized nanocomposite paper achieves an ultrahigh breakdown strength of 125.63 kV mm −1 , markedly exceeding commercial aramid paper. The nanocomposite paper further retains >80% of its breakdown strength after UV/thermal aging and repeated folding and exhibits enhanced flame retardancy and thermoplastic‐driven reprocessing potential; despite progressive performance attenuation during recycling, recycled samples maintain breakdown strength superior to commercial aramid paper, benefiting from the thermoplastic re‐weldability of the PAR network. “Simulation‐to‐data‐to‐manufacturing” paradigm provides a quantitative route for designing polymer dielectrics with controllable performance and scalable processability.

papers.title: Substrate-dependent control of bioprinted hiPSC deposition and colony formation
papers.abstract: Human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) are widely used for disease modelling, drug screening, and tissue engineering. However, their culture is highly sensitive to seeding conditions and prone to operator-dependent variability. Bioprinting offers a potential route to standardize early cell seeding and enable spatial control but requires compatible substrates to support cell attachment and maintain pluripotency. Bioprinted deposition of hiPSCs was evaluated as a controlled seeding strategy. To promote cell attachment during bioprinting, three positively charged surface coatings (polyethyleneimine (PEI), poly-D-lysine (PDL), and poly-L-lysine (PLL)) were assessed. Post-deposition, cell attachment, viability, and pluripotency-associated characteristics were analyzed. The ability to generate spatially defined colonies was tested using patterned depositions through bioprinting. Surface coating had a pronounced effect on hiPSC behavior following bioprinting. Among the tested conditions, low concentrations of PLL provided the best overall performance, supporting cell recovery, attachment, and colony formation while preserving pluripotency-associated features. In contrast, PDL was associated with reduced maintenance of pluripotency characteristics, indicating limited suitability for hiPSC culture in this context. Patterned depositions on PLLcoated substrates enabled the formation of spatially defined hiPSC colonies. Substrate compatibility is a key determinant of successful bioprinted hiPSC culture. PLL supports controlled seeding, viability, and maintenance of pluripotency, enabling reproducible spatial patterning. This study establishes a practical workflow for bioprinted hiPSC deposition and highlights the importance of surface chemistry in stem cell biofabrication.

papers.title: Influence of Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitors and Serotonin-Norepinephrine Reuptake Inhibitors on Dental Implant Osseointegration and Failure: A Review of Evidence
papers.abstract: Mounting evidence assigns serotonergic signaling a possible part in bone metabolism, which bears on two antidepressant classes in widespread clinical use: selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors and serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors. We assess how these classes affect bone healing, bone quality, peri-implant bone changes, osseointegration, and dental implant failure. PubMed searches identified experimental, clinical, and observational studies that examined antidepressant exposure in relation to dental implant outcomes or bone-related effects. The evidence was weighed separately by antidepressant class and by individual medication. Relevant systematic reviews and meta-analyses were also included. Across clinical studies, selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors show a repeated association with increased dental implant failure, even though the magnitude and timing of the reported risk differ among reports. Greater peri-implant marginal bone loss and altered bone mineral density have likewise been linked to exposure to these agents. Experimentally, their effects on bone healing, bone-implant contact, and osteoblast and osteoclast function support these clinical observations. By contrast, evidence for serotonin norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors is sparse. A single retrospective study tied their use strongly to implant failure, while results for bone mineral density and periodontal outcomes proved less consistent. On current evidence, antidepressant exposure may be associated with altered bone remodeling and dental implant outcomes. Since the clinical literature is largely retrospective and experimental models have inherent limits, no definitive causal conclusions are possible. Prospective, medication-specific clinical studies that account for dosage, treatment duration, underlying psychiatric conditions, and established implant-related risk factors are needed.

papers.title: Comparing the refreshing and single batch powder reuse methods for AlSi7Mg produced by laser powder bed fusion
papers.abstract: Laser powder bed fusion is used primarily to produce metallic components and allows for a high degree of geometric freedom and low material usage, although this is reliant on powder reuse, which is now common practice in industrial and academic settings. However, the methodological details of powder reuse are not regularly considered and so current irregularities in practice have the potential to result in degraded and inconsistent properties for parts manufactured with reused powders. Therefore, this work focuses on a comparison between two powder reuse methods to produce AlSi7Mg parts by laser powder bed fusion: powder refreshing and single batch powder reuse, finding that the powder reuse method influences powder characteristics to a greater extent than mechanical properties. Powder flowability improved for the refreshing method, seeing a 20.3% reduction in Hall flow time over the first four manufacturing runs, while the single batch method changed from non-flowing to flowing powder over the same period. Powder magnesium content also saw a larger decrease during the single batch method of 9.4% compared to 7.1% for the refreshing method. No significant changes to tensile properties were seen for the refreshing method, alongside a minor reduction in high cycle fatigue resistance at a stress amplitude of 200 MPa, whereas no changes in either tensile or fatigue properties were observed for the single batch method. These results show that while powder characteristics are dependent on the powder reuse method changes to the mechanical properties of parts are minimal, indicating both reuse methods are viable powder management strategies. However, different powder batches were used for each powder reuse method which may have influenced the degree to which these changes can be attributed solely to each specific powder reuse method.

papers.title: Re-establishing osseointegration following peri-implantitis: a scoping review of implant surface decontamination methods
papers.abstract: Peri-implantitis is a biofilm-associated inflammatory condition characterised by inflammation of the peri-implant mucosa and progressive loss of supporting bone. Implant surface decontamination is central to its treatment, but it remains uncertain whether decontamination permits re-osseointegration or only contributes to disease resolution. This scoping review mapped the evidence on implant surface decontamination methods and characterised the type of evidence available for re-osseointegration. The review followed the Arksey and O’Malley framework and is reported according to PRISMA-ScR. PubMed, Scopus and Web of Science were searched, with supplementary searching of Google Scholar, for records published from January 2000 to September 2025, and reference lists of included sources were screened. Eligibility was defined with the Population–Concept–Context framework. Sources were charted by design, disease entity, treatment setting, decontamination modality and the highest level of evidence reported for re-osseointegration (histological, radiographic, clinical or laboratory). Of 267 records identified (211 after removal of duplicates), 91 full-text reports were assessed and 55 sources were included: 35 primary studies (12 randomised controlled trials, 12 non-randomised clinical studies, one animal study and 10 in vitro studies) and 20 secondary sources (systematic and narrative reviews and one book chapter). Among primary studies, mechanical decontamination ( n = 8), head-to-head comparisons across modality classes ( n = 8) and laser or photodynamic approaches ( n = 6) were investigated most often. Clinical studies mainly reported probing pocket depth, bleeding on probing, suppuration and marginal bone level. Histological evidence of re-osseointegration was limited to one human case report (four implants; 5.7%–39.0% re-osseointegration) and one canine study; no randomised trial reported histological outcomes. Two clinical studies concerned peri-implant mucositis and therefore could not inform re-osseointegration. Clinical and radiographic improvement after several decontamination protocols is well documented, but direct evidence that any method restores bone-to-implant contact in humans is confined to isolated histological reports. How often a protocol has been investigated does not indicate how effective it is. Future studies should report peri-implantitis and peri-implant mucositis, and surgical and non-surgical settings, separately, and should include histological or other direct measures of re-osseointegration where this is ethically and practically feasible.

papers.title: Bovine Serum Albumin-Crosslinked Silk Fibroin-Based Bioink via Thiol-Ene Click Chemistry for Bone Tissue Engineering.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Methacrylated silk fibroin (Sil-MA) has been widely used as a photocrosslinkable silk-based bioink for light-based bioprinting. However, Sil-MA exhibits limited mechanical strength and limited intrinsic cell-adhesive properties, which restrict its use in mechanically demanding applications such as bone tissue engineering. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes an advanced silk-based bioink that incorporates a protein-based functional crosslinker through thiol-ene click chemistry. METHODS: Norbornene-functionalized silk fibroin (Silk-NB) and thiol-functionalized bovine serum albumin (BSA-SH) were synthesized and crosslinked via thiol-ene photopolymerization to develop protein-based hydrogels aimed at improving mechanical performance and supporting cell attachment. Chemical functionalization was characterized, and the resulting bioinks were evaluated through rheological and mechanical analyses. Printability and shape fidelity were assessed using a 2D grid pattern and a 3D construct. In vitro studies using rabbit bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells (rBMSCs) were performed to evaluate initial cell adhesion, cytoskeletal organization, and osteogenic differentiation. RESULTS: Compared with Sil-MA, the Silk-NB/BSA-SH bioinks exhibited enhanced viscoelastic and compressive properties while maintaining high printing fidelity. The Silk-NB/BSA-SH network also improved initial rBMSC adhesion and cytoskeletal organization. Furthermore, enhanced osteogenic differentiation-associated responses were observed under osteogenic induction conditions, as demonstrated by increased alkaline phosphatase (ALP) activity and mineralization-related responses. CONCLUSION: The Silk-NB/BSA-SH thiol-ene click chemistry bioink presents a design strategy that simultaneously satisfies printability, mechanical performance, and biological functionality. This protein-based functional crosslinking approach addresses key limitations of conventional Sil-MA and supports the potential of the Silk-NB/BSA-SH bioink for digital light processing (DLP)-based bone tissue engineering applications.

papers.title: Mechanical testing and energy absorption of lightweight TPMS porous structures for construction
papers.abstract: Triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) structures are of interest as lightweight cores for protective building components, but their geometric design must balance energy absorption with stable deformation. This study examines the effects of relative density and unit cell size on Gyroid (G) and Diamond (D) structures manufactured from polylactic acid (PLA). Quasi-static compression tests, finite element analysis, and digital image correlation were combined to compare load responses, collapse modes, and energy absorption. Relative densities ranged from 30% to 50%, and unit cell sizes ranged from 6 to 14 mm. Increasing relative density from 30% to 50% raised total energy absorption by 211.23% for G-type structures and 210.77% for D-type structures. The corresponding increases in specific energy absorption were 65.65% and 107.16%. G-type structures collapsed progressively in horizontal layers, whereas D-type structures developed diagonal shear bands and achieved higher total and specific energy absorption within the tested range. In the cell-size series, the number of cells remained fixed, so increasing cell size also enlarged the specimens. The resulting increase in total absorbed energy therefore reflects overall geometric scaling as well as cell size. Larger cells were also associated with earlier densification and less continuous collapse. These results identify a practical trade-off between absorbed energy and deformation stability, and provide a comparative basis for developing TPMS cores for protective construction components.

papers.title: Analysis of factors hindering the prevention of perioperative hypothermia in elderly patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty: A qualitative study
papers.abstract: Background Elderly patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty (THA) have a high incidence of perioperative hypothermia due to anesthetic suppression of thermoregulation, prolonged surgical duration, and diminished endogenous thermoregulatory function, which can lead to poor outcomes. Effective prevention of hypothermia is a critical clinical issue; however, previous studies have lacked in-depth analysis of comprehensive continuous management and practical barriers. Objective This study aimed to identify barriers to the prevention of perioperative hypothermia in elderly THA patients. Methods A qualitative study design was employed, conducted from January to February 2026 at a Grade III Level A hospital in the Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region. Using purposive sampling, anesthesiologists (n = 5), anesthesia nurses (n = 5), and operating room nurses (n = 5) were recruited as participants. Semi-structured face-to-face interviews were conducted, and data were analyzed using content analysis with the assistance of NVivo 12.0 software. Results A total of 3 themes and 5 subthemes were identified: (1) System and process level: The warm chain management process requires improvement, and the allocation of key warming resources needs to be strengthened; (2) Human resources and team atmosphere level: Nursing staffing needs to be reinforced, and a positive organizational culture requires cultivation; (3) Multidisciplinary collaboration and continuous improvement level: The multidisciplinary collaboration platform and continuous improvement system remain inadequate. Conclusion Diverse factors hinder the prevention of perioperative hypothermia in elderly THA patients. Managers should implement improvements across three dimensions—system processes, human resources and team atmosphere, and multidisciplinary collaboration—to explore perioperative temperature management strategies and promote quality improvements in hypothermia prevention and control.

papers.title: Applications of Electromyography in Monitoring Post-Operative Outcomes After Total Hip Arthroplasty
papers.abstract: Electromyography (EMG) measures electrical activity generated by muscle fibers during contraction and has been applied in postoperative total hip arthroplasty (THA) to evaluate gait, muscle and nerve function, assistive devices, and surgical approaches. With primary THA projected to grow 71% by 2030, demand for objective postoperative outcome measures continues to rise. However, literature on EMG’s clinical utility after THA remains limited. This systematic review of EMG applications after THA followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines, searching PubMed, Medical Literature Analysis and Retrieval System Online (MEDLINE), Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and the Physiotherapy Evidence Database for peer-reviewed original research articles in English using EMG for postoperative assessment in THA patients, excluding case reports and studies of non-THA hip surgeries. Data extracted included study design, patient demographics, surgical approach, and reasons and outcomes of EMG use. Thirty-two studies from 1984 to 2025 were analyzed. EMG was applied to assess gait, muscle, and nerve function and recovery, the influence of assistive devices, and differences across surgical approaches. Findings on muscle activation patterns and gait parameters varied widely between studies. EMG identified subclinical nerve injuries, suggested differences in nerve and muscle findings between surgical approaches and allowed comparison of rehabilitation interventions. EMG shows promise as a quantitative tool for assessing postoperative outcomes following THA, particularly for guiding rehabilitation and comparing surgical approaches. However, a routine clinical benefit has not been established, and further high-quality research is needed.

papers.title: Development of an electrified penile implant with wireless control for enhanced user experience
papers.abstract: Erectile dysfunction (ED) is a pervasive condition affecting millions of men worldwide, with an increasing incidence expected over the coming years. Traditional penile implants, though effective, have seen minimal technological advancement over the past few decades, leading to limitations in natural feel, reliability, and ease of use. This thesis explores the integration of soft robotics and electrical engineering principles, particularly micropumps and electronic control systems, into the development of a next-generation penile implant. The goal of this thesis is to design, build, and bench-test a soft robotic penile implant prototype that inflates electrically under wireless smartphone control, replacing the manually squeezed scrotal pump of current devices, and to show that it can reach and hold a physiological target pressure of 100 mmHg. The research systematically evaluates the compatibility and performance of soft robotic components designed for axial and radial expansion within the penile implant. Various prototypes were developed using innovative materials and designs, including a porous structure aimed at minimizing fluid volume while maximizing expansion capacity. Additionally, the study incorporates electrical pressurization systems, calibrated through force-sensitive resistors and controlled wirelessly via a Bluetooth connection, allowing for discreet and convenient operation through a smartphone interface. Bench testing showed that the prototype reached a target pressure of 100 mmHg within 30 seconds under wireless command, removing the repeated manual actuation required by conventional pump systems. A constraining shell analogous to the tunica albuginea bounds the actuator's expansion. A closed-form hyperelastic analysis developed here shows that such a constraint is not merely cosmetic: an unconstrained elastomeric wall of these dimensions cannot sustain the physiological target pressure at any stretch, across the full plausible range of geometry and material stiffness. As a bench-scale feasibility study, carried out with non-implantable hardware and without human or animal subjects, this work establishes a control architecture that can inform the future development of implantable devices of this class.

papers.title: ELECTRICAL CIRCUIT INFLUENCE ON THE RESPONSE OF STRUCTURALLY OPTIMIZED PIEZOELECTRIC HARVESTERS
papers.abstract: The paper investigates the influence of an electrical circuit on the electrical and mechanical behavior of structurally optimized piezoelectric energy harvesters. A quadmorph cantilever piezoelectric harvester comprising four PZT-5H active layers is analyzed. Structural optimization is pursued by reducing the piezoelectric material towards a triangular longitudinal section, comparing the performance with the original rectangular structure. Finite element simulations have been conducted, employing a digital twin with a full coupling of Solid Mechanics, Electrostatics, and Electrical Circuit physics interfaces. The electrical circuit emulates the finite input impedance of the spectrum analyzer used in the laboratory. Introducing the electrical impedance shifts the response parameters of interest in both mechanical and electrical domains, changing resonant frequency, stress, displacement, and voltage due to electromechanical coupling. The performance of the optimized structures is evaluated in terms of electrical response per unit volume of piezoelectric material under two relevant approaches: the same inertial mass and the same mechanical stress. The results demonstrate that the triangular structure enables a more efficient use of piezoelectric material, while significantly reducing material volume. The simulations with an electrical circuit indicate its potential use for fine-tuning.

papers.title: Experimental–Finite Element Method Confounding in Machine Learning Predictions of Shear Capacity for Reinforced Deep Beams with Web Openings
papers.abstract: Machine learning (ML) models trained on pooled experimental and finite element method (FEM) data may achieve high accuracy without reliable generalization to independent experimental studies. This study evaluates the ultimate shear capacity of 498 reinforced concrete deep beams with web openings (201 experimental and 297 FEM specimens) using Monte Carlo validation, SHAP analysis, leave-one-original-study-out (LOSO) validation, and conformal prediction. The baseline models use nine parameters: a/H, ax/a, ay/H, Xo/a, Yo/H, ρsw, ρs, fc′, and fy. The FEM specimens contain square web openings, whereas the experimental dataset includes different opening geometries. Despite high pooled accuracy (R2 ≈ 0.99), substantial differences in geometric scale and response distributions limit its interpretation. In the pooled Random Forest model, the mean absolute SHAP attribution of ρsw was 1234 kN, with opposite mean signed contributions for experimental (−1443 kN) and FEM (+1074 kN) specimens. Sensitivity analyses showed that these attributions depend on model specification and data composition rather than representing direct physical effects. LOSO validation revealed poor cross-study generalization, with median R2 values of −11.503 for Random Forest and −18.233 for tuned XGBoost under pooled training; negative values persisted under experimental-only training. These findings highlight the need for source-specific evaluation, scale-aware modeling, and independent experimental validation before engineering application.

papers.title: A novel bilayer cell-free 3D-printed scaffold for osteochondral defect repair
papers.abstract: Articular cartilage defects are difficult to repair due to inferior regenerative capacity and complex structural integration between cartilage and subchondral bone. Conventional clinical treatments often cause fibrocartilage formation and unsatisfactory long-term outcomes. To address these limitations, we developed a bilayer, cell-free osteochondral scaffold fabricated by low-temperature extrusion-based 3D printing using gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA). The cartilage layer was functionalized with dopamine-modified hyaluronic acid (DHA) to enhance bone marrow mesenchymal stem cell (BMSC) migration and chondrogenic differentiation in vitro. The subchondral bone layer incorporated nano-hydroxyapatite (nHAp) to provide osteoinductive cues and mechanical support for bone regeneration. The physicochemical properties, printability, mechanical performance, and biocompatibility of the scaffolds were systematically characterized. In vitro studies demonstrated that the GelMA/DHA layer significantly enhanced BMSCs migration and upregulated chondrogenic markers, while the GelMA/nHAp layer promoted osteogenic differentiation. In a rabbit osteochondral defect model, the bilayer scaffold facilitated coordinated regeneration of hyaline-like cartilage and subchondral bone, as evidenced by gross evaluation, micro-computed tomography analysis, and histological staining. This spatially organized, cell-free strategy combines complementary cartilage- and bone-supportive cues and promotes coordinated osteochondral repair. The proposed bilayer scaffold offers a promising biomaterial-based approach for osteochondral defect repair without exogenous cell transplantation.

papers.title: An interpretable hybrid FELA–boosting framework for predicting pullout capacity of rectangular buried pipelines in dense sand
papers.abstract: Accurately predicting the pullout capacity of buried rectangular pipelines in dense sand remains a significant challenge because of the complex interaction between pipeline geometry, stress-dependent soil behavior, and failure mechanism development. This study combines Finite Element Limit Analysis (FELA), the Bolton model, and gradient-boosting machine learning algorithms to evaluate the normalized pullout capacity factor (Nγ). The parametric study varied the embedment ratio (H/B), aspect ratio (L/B), soil unit weight (γ), relative density (DR), particle crushing strength (Q), and critical-state friction angle (ϕcv). The results show that geometric parameters dominate the uplift response, with higher H/B increasing confinement and larger L/B promoting wider plastic failure zones. Soil parameters influence the response through stress-dependent dilatancy, where higher DR, Q, and ϕcv increase Nγ, whereas higher γ slightly reduces the normalized pullout capacity factor. The 2880-case FELA database generated using Optum G2 was divided into four unit-weight-specific subsets of 720 cases, with separate XGBoost, CatBoost, and LightGBM models developed for each subset. For γ = 20 kN/m3, LightGBM achieved the best performance on the adopted testing split (R2 = 0.9934), while CatBoost achieved the highest training accuracy. SHAP analysis of the XGBoost models and first-order Sobol analysis of the FELA results both identified H/B and L/B as the dominant parameters, although their ordering differed. Overall, the framework provides efficient surrogate estimates of FELA-derived pullout capacity and interpretable parameter trends within the investigated ranges.

papers.title: Improving tumor models: investigating co-culture and bioink maturation in 3D-Bioprinted melanoma constructs
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional bioprinting enables spatially defined melanoma models in which tumor cell behavior can be examined within controlled hydrogel microenvironments. Here, we compared two alginate-based bioinks that support contrasting melanoma phenotypes: pre-crosslinked alginate dialdehyde-gelatin (ADA-GEL) and an alginate-nanocellulose bioink (Cellink Bioink). Mel Im and Mel Wei cells were bioprinted as monocultures or co-cultured with adipose-derived stem cells (ADSC). Cell-cycle state, survival, metabolic activity, colony formation, cytoskeletal morphology, and melanoma-cell proliferation were evaluated. Hydrogel microstructure, printability, acellular mass retention, and mechanical properties of cast specimens over the 14-day culture period were also assessed. Cellink Bioink maintained predominantly viable, G1-phase melanoma cells with limited HMB45/Ki67 colocalization and colony formation, consistent with a dormancy-like phenotype. In contrast, ADA-GEL supported higher metabolic activity, cell-cycle progression, colony formation, and the formation of Ki67-positive melanoma-cell clusters. Co-culture-associated responses varied by melanoma cell line and seeding concentration rather than showing a uniformly stimulatory or inhibitory pattern. Over 14 days, Cellink Bioink showed transient stiffening with limited acellular mass loss, whereas ADA-GEL progressively softened and showed greater acellular mass loss. The presence of Mel Im cells was associated with differences in the mechanical responses of both bioinks. These findings establish complementary 3D-bioprinted melanoma models for investigating proliferative and dormancy-like states and demonstrate that tumor cell behavior and co-culture-associated responses depend on the surrounding bioink microenvironment.

papers.title: Mismatch Between Rotational and Linear Speed Affects Primary Stability of Dental Implants: An Experimental Study
papers.abstract: Introduction Rotational and linear insertion speeds must be synchronized to ensure proper dental implant advancement. This study investigated the effects of a mismatch between rotational and linear speeds during implant insertion on primary stability. Methods Thirty identical dental implants were inserted into synthetic and natural bone at a constant rotational speed of 25 rpm. Correct insertion (CI) was defined as synchronized rotational and linear speeds. Accelerated insertion (AI) referred to a higher linear speed relative to the rotational speed. Primary stability was evaluated using maximum insertion torque (MIT), implant stability quotient (ISQ), and push-in test parameters. Results In natural bone, correct insertion produced significantly higher primary stability than accelerated insertion, as measured by MIT ( P < .001), ISQ ( P = .013), bone–implant construct stiffness ( P = .019), and maximum push-in force ( P < .001). In synthetic bone, no significant differences in stability indicators were found between insertion protocols, but axial force in the AI group was significantly higher compared to the CI group ( P = .013). For correct insertion in natural bone, a positive correlation was found between MIT and maximum push-in force (ρ = 0.867, P = .015). In contrast, no other correlation among stability indicators was statistically significant. Conclusion Mismatch between linear and rotational insertion speeds was associated with reduced primary stability in natural bone and increased axial force in synthetic bone. Clinical relevance Monitoring axial force during implant insertion, particularly in low-density bone, may provide valuable feedback on insertion accuracy, but requires further investigation.

papers.title: Dual Active Learning for Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
papers.abstract: Aligning large language models (LLMs) with human preferences is critical to recent advances in generative artificial intelligence. Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) is widely applied to achieve this objective. A key step in RLHF is to learn the reward function from human feedback. However, human feedback is costly and time-consuming, making it essential to collect high-quality conversation data for human teachers to label. Additionally, different human teachers have different levels of expertise. It is thus critical to query the most appropriate teacher for their opinions. In this paper, we use offline reinforcement learning (RL) to formulate the alignment problem. Motivated by the idea of $D$-optimal design, we first propose a dual active reward learning algorithm for the simultaneous selection of conversations and teachers. Next, we apply pessimistic RL to solve the alignment problem, based on the learned reward estimator. Theoretically, we show that the reward estimator obtained through our proposed adaptive selection strategy achieves minimal generalized variance asymptotically, and prove that the sub-optimality of our pessimistic policy scales as $O(1/\sqrt{T})$ with a given sample budget $T$. Through simulations and experiments on LLMs, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our algorithm and its superiority over state-of-the-art.

papers.title: An introduction to zero-order optimization techniques for robotics
papers.abstract: Zero-order optimization techniques are becoming increasingly popular in robotics due to their ability to handle non-differentiable functions and escape local minima. These advantages make them particularly useful for trajectory optimization and policy optimization. In this work, we propose a mathematical tutorial on random search. It offers a simple and unifying perspective for understanding a wide range of algorithms commonly used in robotics. Leveraging this viewpoint, we classify many trajectory optimization methods under a common framework and derive novel competitive RL algorithms.

papers.title: Tailoring germanium heterostructures for quantum devices with machine learning
papers.abstract: Germanium (Ge) quantum wells are emerging as versatile platforms for quantum devices, supporting high-quality spin qubits and integration with superconducting leads. These applications benefit from strong intrinsic spin-orbit interaction (SOI), enabling efficient electrical control and engineering of spin degrees of freedom. The most advanced Ge/SiGe heterostructures to date, based on compressively strained Ge channels within strain-relaxed silicon-germanium (SiGe) barriers, exhibit weak SOI due to the heavy-hole character of the wave function, posing challenges for spin-based quantum devices and requiring complex device designs for fast qubit manipulation. In this work, we demonstrate that concrete heterostructure modifications can overcome these limitations, enhancing SOI by up to three orders of magnitude. Specifically, we propose to enrich unstrained Ge channels by localized, strained silicon spikes. Leveraging a multi-objective Bayesian optimization, we optimize the spike profile to maximize SOI, while ensuring compatibility with current epitaxial growth processes and robustness against realistic variations of growth parameters. Our heterostructure substantially enhances device performance, yielding up to two orders of magnitude higher quantum-dot spin qubit quality factors than state-of-the-art materials. We also predict GHz-scale spin splittings for hybrid superconducting Andreev spin qubits. These novel Ge heterostructures with engineered Si concentration profiles can open pathways to scalable quantum and spintronic applications.

papers.title: An efficient framework for robust sample size determination
papers.abstract: In many settings, robust data analysis involves computational methods for uncertainty quantification and statistical inference. To design frequentist studies that leverage robust analysis methods, suitable sample sizes to achieve desired power are often found by estimating sampling distributions of p -values via intensive simulation. Moreover, most sample size recommendations rely heavily on assumptions about a single data-generating process. Consequently, robustness in data analysis does not by itself imply robustness in study design, as examining sample size sensitivity to data-generating assumptions typically requires further simulations. We propose an economical alternative for determining sample sizes that are robust to multiple data-generating mechanisms. Applying our theoretical results that model p -values as a function of the sample size, we assess power across the sample size space using simulations conducted at only two sample sizes for each data-generating mechanism. We demonstrate the broad applicability of our methodology to study design based on M-estimators in both experimental and observational settings through a varied set of clinical examples.

papers.title: Combining gravitational wave search pipelines to find subthreshold signals in GWTC-5.0
papers.abstract: The detection of transient gravitational wave signals relies on independent search algorithms that analyse detector data and assign significance measures to candidate events. However, varying performance complicates their interpretation. We use supervised machine learning combined with conformal prediction, a framework to quantify uncertainties, to merge multi-pipeline information into well-calibrated confidence scores. We demonstrate that this approach is robust across different classifier architectures and remains stable when trained on different simulated datasets. When applied to events across the GWTC catalogue up to and including the second part of the fourth observing run, the framework identifies several subthreshold candidates with elevated confidence, including the binary neutron star candidate GW200311_103121. We examine the reliability of these up-rankings, finding evidence that high-confidence predictions correspond to signal-like events. This framework enables simplified systematic candidate assessment for gravitational wave catalogues and real-time alerts by providing a single, well-calibrated confidence measure per candidate.

papers.title: DFlee: a scalable agent-based framework for simulating flood-induced population displacement across multiple flood scenarios
papers.abstract: Natural disasters displace millions of people each year, and effective disaster response requires accurate models of population movement. This study presents DFlee, an agent-based model for flood-induced evacuation built on the Flee framework for conflict-driven displacement. DFlee introduces three key extensions: (i) dynamic integration of evolving, location-specific flood conditions into agent decision-making; (ii) risk-sensitive destination selection accounting for flood severity, shelter inundation risk, and accessibility; and (iii) recession-driven short-term return-to-origin. Synthetic scenarios with recurrence intervals ranging from 10 to over 100 years represent minor and major riverine floods, coastal storm surges, and compound flooding. Validation combines empirical comparison against the 2022 Bauchi flood in Nigeria with behavioural validation of three stylised facts: preference for nearby safe destinations, short-term return to origin as flood conditions improve, and heterogeneous evacuation timing. Across scenarios, approximately 84–91% of evacuees select the nearest safe destination, while returns to origin begin promptly as flood conditions recede, with cumulative returns within the simulated window limited by late-peaking displacement dynamics. These behaviours persist across a tenfold increase in population size, and ARCHER2 experiments simulate 16 million agents in under one minute on a single compute node and around five seconds on 32 nodes, supporting uncertainty quantification, scenario exploration, and humanitarian planning.

papers.title: Comparative analysis of nonlinear state estimators within fractional model predictive control for a fractional chaotic Rössler System
papers.abstract: This paper presents a robust state estimation and control framework for a fractional-order Rössler system using fractional model predictive control integrated with nonlinear state observers. The system dynamics are modeled using the Grünwald-Letnikov fractional derivative, which enables efficient numerical implementation while capturing inherent memory effects. The proposed framework incorporates and systematically compares three nonlinear estimation techniques: the Extended Kalman Filter, the Unscented Kalman Filter, and the Particle Filter. These observers are evaluated within the predictive control loop under partial state measurement scenarios, including the estimation of unmeasured states from limited outputs. The study considers realistic operating conditions with additive Gaussian noise and investigates estimation accuracy, robustness to disturbances, and computational cost. Quantitative performance metrics such as root mean square error and convergence behavior are used to assess the performance of each estimator. Results demonstrate that while the Extended Kalman Filter offers computational efficiency, the Unscented Kalman Filter improves estimation accuracy for strongly nonlinear dynamics, and the Particle Filter provides enhanced robustness under higher noise levels at the expense of increased computational effort. The findings highlight the trade-offs between estimation performance and computational complexity, offering practical insights for selecting suitable observers in fractional-order chaotic systems controlled via predictive strategies.

papers.title: Impact of elemental segregation on active and transpassive corrosion phenomenology of additively manufactured 316L
papers.abstract: The active and transpassive dissolution behaviors of additively manufactured (AM) laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) and direct energy deposition (DED) 316L stainless steels were evaluated using ASTM standard methods as well as electrochemical and microscopy characterization techniques. Conventional wrought 316L and 317L was used as baselines for chemical, microstructure, and electrochemical behavior. It was discovered that both LPBF and DED induce non-equilibrium solidification conditions that lead to elemental segregation of Cr, Ni, and Mo. The segregation occurs at cellular dendritic walls in LPBF and within the ferrite phase in DED, whereas wrought materials exhibit a homogeneous microstructure and elemental distribution. Under active dissolution in the presence of acidic (H 2 SO 4 ) and depassivating species (KSCN), cellular dendritic interiors and melt pool boundaries undergo selective attack in LPBF while austenite dissolves faster than ferrite in DED. Conversely, when transpassive dissolution occurs, cellular dendritic walls are attacked in LPBF, and ferrite is attacked in DED. When LPBF processing parameters are optimized for density, the corrosion rate (ASTM A262 Practice B) was the lowest in comparison to wrought 316L and 317L. Samples with the highest corrosion rate correlated to the presence of lack-of-fusion porosity (1.8% porosity) or a large grain structure (DED).

papers.title: Outlier-robust dynamic force reconstruction in nonsmooth structural dynamics: A computational generalized-adjoint and primal-dual framework
papers.abstract: Force estimates obtained from vibration measurements can absorb errors caused by sensor contamination and an incomplete structural model. This study examines both effects using an ℓ 1 acceleration misfit and a piecewise-smooth structural model. A generalized Gauss–Newton method computes force updates through local convex subproblems solved by the alternating direction method of multipliers. The continuous-time adjoint motivates this discrete formulation but does not establish global optimality. Three synthetic benchmarks consider unilateral contact, breathing-stiffness switching, and simultaneous beam loads. With fixed parameter settings, nonlinear ℓ 1 reconstruction gives relative force errors of 0.280, 0.054, and 0.126. Further beam comparisons select regularization from withheld measurements and include innovation-clipped Kalman smoothing, a residual-based physics-informed neural network, and a neural force model that enforces the discrete dynamics exactly. The latter gives lower force errors on two of three noise realizations. The batch method requires less time for refitting, but not when parameter selection is included. Refining the internal time step reduces the known-force response error from 1.69 × 10 −3 to 4.34 × 10 −6 against an independent continuous-model solution, with unchanged observation and force grids. These results show the value of combining outlier-resistant fitting with the relevant structural physics, while also showing the limits of response-based parameter selection and finite-budget optimization. The evidence is numerical and applies to continuous piecewise-linear restoring forces rather than impulsive contact or arbitrary discontinuities.

papers.title: Physical Activity Interventions Embedded Within University Teaching and Learning: A Scoping Review
papers.abstract: Embedding physical activity into the university curriculum offers a way to address students’ typically high sedentary behaviour. While some interventions have been trialled, the heterogeneity of methods precludes synthesis of results. This review aimed to document the methods used for assessing embedded physical activity or sedentary behaviour interventions to summarise existing research and identify methodological gaps. Four databases were searched for peer-reviewed articles. Of the 7345 citations screened, 28 studies were included, describing two intervention types: active breaks (n = 15), involving short movement breaks, and physically active learning (n = 13), involving active workstations (e.g., sit-stand desks). Small-sample feasibility studies were common and quality-assessment ratings often were low. Outcome measures included physical activity, academic performance, and feasibility. Few studies collected qualitative data or investigated teaching staffs’ experiences. To better inform design, implementation, and evaluation of future evidence-based interventions, carefully controlled studies engaging a range of university stakeholders are needed.

papers.title: Debate-Based Learning in Postgraduate Medical Education: A Narrative Review of the Evidence Base, Challenges, and Future Directions
papers.abstract: Debate is an active pedagogical practice in which learners must evaluate evidence, defend positions within a topic, and respond to criticism from the opposing view. Within the postgraduate medical education environment, traditional didactic teaching methods such as lectures have traditionally constituted the principal educational approach despite growing recognition of the value of active and learner-centred educational strategies. Debate-based learning represents an active learning and drives self-directed learning through intrinsic motivation and preparation. In the postgraduate medical education context, debate offers an opportunity for learners to engage with critical thinking and evidence appraisal within a clinical setting. This narrative review critically examines the theoretical foundations, existing evidence base, practical considerations, and limitations of debate-based learning in a postgraduate medical education setting, highlighting the potential of debate as a learner-centred approach to developing critical appraisal, clinical reasoning, and professional communication skills required for a modern clinician.

papers.title: The evolution of population spatialisation in the era of big data and artificial intelligence: a systematic review
papers.abstract: Population spatialisation serves as a critical nexus transforming aggregated population counts into spatially explicit population distributions, providing an essential foundation for urban planning, disaster management, and public health assessment. However, the inherent complexity of human settlement patterns presents significant challenges for population spatialisation and fine-grained population disaggregation. With the convergence of geospatial big data and artificial intelligence (AI), population spatialisation has undergone rapid changes in data sources, spatial representations, and modelling approaches, yet its evolution has received limited systematic attention. To address this gap, this paper reviews the evolution of population spatialisation through a structured literature synthesis complemented by bibliometric analysis, tracing its development from traditional redistribution approaches to recent AI-enabled methods, with a particular focus on emerging geospatial foundation models. Furthermore, the synthesis reveals a methodological transition from rule-based redistribution towards data-driven, probabilistic, and representation-learning approaches, coupled with the progressive diversification of spatial representations and growing attention to temporally explicit and demographically differentiated population estimation. Based on these findings, future research should prioritise robustness across scales and contexts, interpretability, uncertainty quantification, and the representation of demographic heterogeneity. Through this review, we aim to elucidate the key transitions in the evolution of population spatialisation, thereby facilitating the development and evaluation of more reliable and demographically informative spatial population products.

papers.title: Impact of prior lower extremity arthroplasty on outcomes following lumbar fusion: a retrospective cohort study
papers.abstract: Study design Retrospective cohort study Objective To assess the impact of a prior total hip arthroplasty (THA) or total knee arthroplasty (TKA) on outcomes following lumbar fusion. Methods Adult patients undergoing elective lumbar fusion between 2017 and 2023 were retrospectively identified and categorized into lower extremity surgery (LES) and no-LES cohorts. Patients were divided into those with a prior history of LES versus those with no prior history of LES and were matched 3:1 using nearest-neighbor propensity score matching based on age, sex, BMI, levels fused, and smoking status. Covariate balance between the matched groups was confirmed following matching. PROMs, including VAS Back/Leg, SF-12, and ODI, were collected preoperatively and at 3, 6, and 12 months postoperatively. A subgroup analysis was performed to directly compare outcomes between prior THA versus TKA. Results Clinical outcomes, including discharge disposition, readmissions, and revisions, were similar between the LES and no-LES groups. At one year, patients with prior LES reported higher ODI scores (27.3 vs. 22.0, P = 0.012) and had less improvement from baseline compared to patients without prior LES (Δ − 15.06 vs. − 23.70, P = 0.021). A similar decrease in ODI improvement was seen at 3 months ( P = 0.041). All other PROMs were comparable at every timepoint. In the subgroup analysis, clinical outcomes did not differ between the THA and TKA cohorts. However, at 1 year postoperatively, patients with a prior TKA reported significantly higher VAS Leg scores compared to THA patients (4.85 vs. 2.62, P = 0.010). This was reinforced by a smaller improvement from baseline in the TKA group (− 1.40 vs. − 4.47, P = 0.035). Conclusion A history of lower extremity arthroplasty did not negatively impact overall clinical or most patient-reported outcomes following a subsequent lumbar fusion, though prior LES was associated with higher disability scores and less improvement in disability at one year. Patients with a prior TKA experienced significantly greater leg pain compared to those with a prior THA at 1 year postoperatively. These findings highlight the importance of considering prior TKA as a potential contributor to postoperative leg pain and may help inform preoperative counseling and interpretation of patient-reported outcomes following lumbar fusion. Level of evidence III.

papers.title: Nonlinear model predictive control for railway stabilization operation based on spatial-domain receding horizon optimization
papers.abstract: With the rapid expansion of high-speed and heavy-haul railways in China, traditional railway stabilization operations—an open-loop approach heavily dependent on worker experience—are increasingly unable to meet the growing demands of railway maintenance in terms of both efficiency and quality. This paper presents the working principle of railway stabilization in detail and proposes, for the first time, a nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) strategy based on spatial-domain receding-horizon optimization. Specifically, using the MFBD and DEM theories together with the Box-Behnken experimental design method, the evolution laws of the mechanical properties of an initially stable ballast bed under variable stabilization conditions are simulated. A nonlinear time-varying model of the lateral resistance of the ballast bed is established by a hybrid modeling approach combining polynomial response surface methodology (RSM) and a deep neural network. Subsequently, in view of the spatially moving characteristics of railway stabilization operations, an NMPC architecture integrating queue state management, constraint prioritization, and spatial-domain receding-horizon optimization is proposed. Finally, simulation and experimental results show that after NMPC operation, the average lateral resistance of the ballast bed reaches 14 kN, the one-pass compliance rate exceeds 90%, the operation time is reduced by 40%, and the improvement rate of lateral resistance is 2.4 times that of traditional operations. Compared with traditional operation methods, the proposed control strategy achieves better improvement in the quality state of the ballast bed and higher operational efficiency. The findings of this study can provide guidance for scientific stabilization operations and promote the theoretical development of railway maintenance.

papers.title: AI-Driven Cross-Scale Simulation of Lithium Batteries
papers.abstract: The evolution of lithium battery performance involves complex coupled processes across multiple scales, ranging from electronic and atomic scales to mesoscopic structures and battery systems. Traditional simulation approaches face significant challenges in accurately predicting realistic battery electrochemical responses because of scale-bridging limitations, high computational costs, and insufficient dynamic feedback mechanisms. In recent years, advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have provided opportunities for cross-scale simulations by enabling knowledge transfer and intelligent prediction through learning physical representations from data. This Review provides a comprehensive overview of AI-driven cross-scale simulation for lithium batteries. The review first discusses AI-enabled simulation approaches spanning the micro- to mesoscale, including machine learning potentials (MLPs), AI-driven kinetic Monte Carlo (AI-kMC), AI-driven phase-field modeling (AI-PFM), and AI-driven coarse-grained molecular dynamics (AI-CGMD). It then summarizes meso- to macroscale methodologies, including surrogate models, reduced-order modeling, and physics-informed neural networks (PINNs). Furthermore, AI applications in multiscale feature fusion, inverse materials design, and battery design automation (BDA) are discussed together with computational paradigms toward digital twins and intelligent battery research and development. Despite substantial advances, several critical challenges, including limited model generalization and insufficient uncertainty quantification, remain. Integrating foundation models, generative AI, and multiscale physical modeling could enable more accurate and computationally efficient battery simulation frameworks. These advances may accelerate the discovery, optimization, and deployment of next-generation energy-storage technologies.

papers.title: LETd-dependent RBE conversion between LEM1- and mMKM-based dose systems and characterisation of LETd-dependent uncertainty in carbon ion radiotherapy
papers.abstract: Background and Aims. Differences between LEM1- and mMKM-based clinical dose systems complicate the translation of RBE-weighted dose in carbon ion radiotherapy, while uncertainties associated with RBE model parameterisation complicate the interpretation of predicted RBE. This work establishes two complementary dose-averaged LET (LET d )-based frameworks to (i) analytically convert RBE between the two systems and (ii) characterise systematic fitting uncertainties and their propagation into RBE. Methods. Monte Carlo simulations of clinical carbon‑ion pencil beams and SOBPs in water were performed using GATE 10/Geant4.11.3.2 within the IDEAL 2 platform. LET d , mixed-beam radiosensitivity α mix , and RBE distributions were computed for both clinical dose systems. Ion-specific α Z,E tables were obtained from saturation-corrected dose-averaged specific energy z * 1D and intrinsic coefficient α z tables computed by internally developed PRUDENT code. Relationship between ε α and ε RBE , which quantify the mMKM-LEM1 relative differences in α mix and RBE, respectively, was derived and approximated using linear functions. The ε α (LET d ) relationship was fitted from simulated α mix and LET d . The full analytical framework was validated in SOBP target regions against computed ε RBE . Systematic fitting uncertainty in mMKM, denoted as η RBE , was characterized by comparing simulated α mix with published in vitro α fit reference at equal LET d , and evaluated for physical dose D=0-8 Gy. Main results. The ε α ranged from -20% at LET d =33 keV/μm to 18% at LET d =95 keV/μm in the target region of SOBP, well described by a logarithmic-logistic form. The linear approximation ε RBE =k·ε α +b predicted the ε RBE within ±1% when ε α was known, and within 3-4% when fitted ε α (LET d ) was used. Large η α was observed, reaching 275% at LET d =22.5 keV/μm and decreasing to -22% at LET d =137 keV/μm. The resulting η RBE exceeded 100% in the low-D-low-LET d region. Significance. This work provides the first closed-form, LET d -based frameworks for RBE conversion in LEM1- and mMKM-based clinical systems and LET d -related uncertainty quantification in the latter. The results reveal the mechanistic link between LET d and ε α and between LET d and η α arising from particle LET spectra, and support LET d -informed plan evaluation.

papers.title: Explainable ensemble learning for chloride penetration (RCPT) and carbonation of concrete: comparative cross-mechanism interpretation with uncertainty quantification
papers.abstract: Chloride ingress and carbonation drive reinforcement corrosion but are usually predicted separately. Explainable ensemble machine learning models were developed for the rapid chloride penetration test (RCPT) charge passed and carbonation depth under a common protocol to compare their governing factors. Literature databases were screened to 145 RCPT records (20 sources) and 2012 carbonation records (45 sources). Five ensembles, including extra trees (ET) and extreme gradient boosting (XGB), were tuned by Bayesian optimization and benchmarked against linear, kernel and power-law models using hold-out testing, repeated 10 × 5-fold cross-validation (CV) and studywise validation. Conformal prediction intervals quantified uncertainty, and Shapley additive explanations and partial dependence interpreted model behavior. XGB predicted carbonation best (R2 = 0.815; RMSE = 3.64 mm; CV R2 = 0.797 ± 0.028), significantly outperforming all others. For RCPT, ET had the highest hold-out accuracy (R2 = 0.791; RMSE = 677.6 C), while ensembles performed comparably in CV. 95% intervals covered 96.6% (RCPT) and 96.3% (carbonation) of test observations. Water-to-binder ratio and binder-related inputs influenced both indicators; exposure conditions dominated carbonation, and ablation showed binder type governs RCPT. Studywise validation limited their use to the represented sources. A durability index combining both predictions outlined data needs for mix design.

papers.title: Voltage Regulation Strategy for Distribution Networks Based on the Dual-Layer World Model and Reinforcement Learning Algorithm
papers.abstract: The high penetration of residential distributed energy resources (RDERs) in distribution networks exhibits high randomness and spatiotemporal coupling, which may cause voltage fluctuations. Although multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (MADRL) enables collaborative control, its reliance on extensive real-world interaction data increases training costs and operational risks. To address these challenges, a collaborative voltage regulation strategy, termed DWM-MATD3, is developed by integrating MADRL with a dual-layer world model (DWM). The upper layer models distribution-network power-flow dynamics using a heterogeneous graph attention network and gated recurrent units (HGAT-GRU), thereby capturing network topology, temporal dependencies, and physical power-flow constraints. The lower layer models residential-device behavior using MLP-GRU networks to improve virtual-environment fidelity. A three-stage training scheme comprising real-data pretraining, real-virtual interaction fine-tuning, and hybrid-data training reduces dependence on real-world data. Parameter sharing further narrows the simulation-to-reality gap and improves sample efficiency. Experiments on modified IEEE 33-bus, 141-bus, and 322-bus systems demonstrate that DWM-MATD3 consistently outperforms the baselines in terms of voltage-violation rate and line loss, with its performance gains increasing as the system scale expands. The testing results demonstrate that the presented DWM-MATD3 method significantly improves the voltage regulation performance in distribution networks with residential distributed energy resources.

papers.title: Characterization of L-PBF Printed AISI 316L Parts: Dimensional accuracy, surface quality, microstructural and mechanical behaviors
papers.abstract: This study investigates components manufactured using low volumetric energy density (VED) in laser powder bed fusion (L-PBF) additive manufacturing, specifically for preliminary prototyping. In industrial contexts, tangible prototypes play a vital role in identifying potential design flaws before assembly and production. To evaluate the influence of low and high VEDs, AISI 316L stainless steel specimens were produced at two speeds while maintaining constant laser power: 300 mm/s and 1500 mm/s, corresponding to VEDs of 80 J/mm³ (high-VED) and 16 J/mm³ (low-VED), respectively. Only the scanning speed was varied, while the laser power (90 W), hatch distance (150 µm), and layer thickness (25 µm) were kept constant. The effect of scanning speed, expressed through VED, was evaluated on four responses: geometric accuracy, surface roughness, porosity, and mechanical properties. Increasing VED from 16 to 80 J/mm³ increased the flatness deviation of all matchbox specimens, mostly for the 2.3 mm-thick specimen (from approximately 1.71% to 6.96%), and increased the angular deviation of the triangular prisms by approximately 1.18–6.88 pp, depending on the angle. In contrast, circularity deviations decreased slightly for all cylindrical features, with the largest decrease observed on the outer surface of the smaller hollow tube (with an inner radius of 1.4 mm and an outer radius of 2.3 mm) from 5.05% to 4.07%, while cylindricity exhibited a more geometry-dependent response for the same tube, decreasing from 30.45% to 28.81%. Surface roughness decreased by approximately 40% at higher VED, with Ra decreasing from 13.41 to 8.03 µm for the dogbone specimens and from 17.05 to 9.98 µm for the hemisphere specimens. Micro-computed tomography revealed substantially higher XCT-resolved porosity in the low-VED specimen (~1.49%) compared with the high-VED specimen (0.17%). Tensile testing showed that the specimen produced at 80 J/mm³ achieved an ultimate tensile strength of 684.0 ± 7.2 MPa, compared with 120.5 ± 16.2 MPa for the specimen produced at 16 J/mm³, corresponding to an approximately 5.7-fold increase. Under the low-VED condition, flatness deviations ranged from approximately 1.71% to 6.11% and angular deviations from 4.68% to 15.16%. The fivefold increase in scanning speed reduces scanning time but compromises density, surface quality, and strength. Therefore, the suitability of this condition for preliminary prototyping should be assessed against the dimensional tolerances and functional requirements of the intended application rather than assumed to be universally acceptable. papers.title: Deconvoluting the biomedical data sciences: A shared framework for clinical and translational research
papers.abstract: Introduction: Clinical and translational research increasingly depends on multidisciplinary teams with specialized data expertise, yet the term data science carries markedly different meanings across fields and institutions. This conceptual ambiguity affects team science, training, and research rigor. We propose a shared framework for the biomedical data sciences: biostatistics, epidemiology, bioinformatics, informatics, and computational biology, grounded in foundational principles common across disciplines. Methods: We trace the historical evolution of the biomedical data sciences, characterize heterogeneity in training across disciplines, and present survey evidence from ACTS BERD and Informatics Special Interest Group members ( n = 88, August 2025) documenting variation in how the term is used and who claims it. Results: Survey respondents varied widely in whether they identified as data scientists and how they defined data science, even within a community of practitioners sharing institutional homes. We interpret this variation not as confusion to be corrected, but as evidence that the singular term obscures distinct disciplines with a broad spectrum of academic traditions. This motivates our proposal: a framework built on what these disciplines share rather than what divides them. Conclusions: The heterogeneity of the biomedical data sciences is a feature of a maturing field, not a problem to be eliminated. A shared framework built on common foundational principles, including matching scientific questions to: appropriate analytic goals, study design, uncertainty quantification, bias mitigation, and reproducibility, offers a path toward more intentional training, earlier engagement of data expertise, and stronger interdisciplinary collaboration in clinical and translational research.

papers.title: Comparison of Rule-Based Natural Language Processing and Diagnosis Code Approaches to Detecting Bleeding in the Electronic Health Record: Algorithm Validation Within a Retrospective Cohort Study
papers.abstract: Background: Anticoagulant use is prevalent and increasing. High-quality anticoagulation management balances individual thrombotic and bleeding risks to optimize care. An automated algorithm to accurately extract major bleeding events from the electronic health record (EHR) of a large health care system would be extremely useful for tracking outcomes of anticoagulated patients. Objective: The study aims to assess the accuracy of a natural language processing (NLP) approach, compared with and in conjunction with a diagnosis code (Dx Code)-based strategy, for detecting major bleeding from the EHR. Methods: Patients with at least 1 prescription for apixaban, dabigatran, edoxaban, rivaroxaban, or warfarin between January 1, 2019, and December 31, 2023, were analyzed for major bleeding events. Major bleeding was defined similarly to the International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis definition. For the NLP algorithm, clinical notes and radiology reports were screened for mentions of bleeding. MedTagger, an open-source, rule-based NLP tool, was then used on the notes. The NLP results were transformed into a feature set, which was used to create a support vector machine model. Three NLP models were created for central nervous system bleeding, critical site bleeding, and bleeding with a hemoglobin drop or transfusions (other major bleeding). Training and test datasets were created using an active learning approach. The model was trained using 80% of the dataset, while the remaining 20% was used for testing. After model finalization, an independent random sample was used to validate the model. Dx Codes were also used to detect major bleeding, similar to previously published approaches. Five unique algorithms were compared: (1) NLP, (2) Dx Code in the primary position, (3) Dx Code in any position, (4) NLP∩Dx Code in any position, and (5) NLP∪Dx Code in any position. All 5 algorithms were compared with manual chart review. Results: -scores for the validation data ranged from 0.509 to 0.679. The NLP∩Dx Code in any position approach yielded excellent precision of 0.864 (95% CI 0.667-0.953) but only 0.559 (95% CI 0.395-0.711) sensitivity. The NLP∪Dx Code in any position approach yielded good sensitivity of 0.824 (95% CI 0.665-0.917) but only 0.368 (95% CI 0.269-0.481) precision. Conclusions: Electronic tools can screen the EHRs to identify major bleeding outcomes in large patient cohorts within a multisite health care network with high precision but only moderate sensitivity. Additional work is needed to enhance sensitivity while maintaining high precision.
